C1_ROUTE_IDENTITY_NORMALIZATION.summary: Route and next-hop identity is compared using non-canonical raw values.

C2_POLICY_RULE_DEPENDENCY.summary: Policy priorities and table dependencies are not validated as one coherent graph.

C3_REVISION_TRANSACTION_FENCING.summary: Revision planning/apply lacks consistent CAS, idempotency and atomic publication.

C4_MANAGEMENT_SAFETY.summary: Protected reachability is not checked against the post-change effective graph.

C5_APPLY_ROLLBACK_RECOVERY.summary: Per-node apply/rollback does not preserve complete last-known-good state.

C6_DRIFT_RECONCILIATION.summary: Desired-observed comparison loses normalization, ownership and freshness boundaries.

C7_FLEET_ROLLOUT.summary: Wave rollout state allows progress or retry on stale/incomplete outcomes.

C8_DEPLOYMENT_AND_UI_CONCURRENCY.summary: Ansible projection and dashboard mutations lack stable idempotency/concurrency contracts.

defects.observable_failure: Equivalent IPv6 prefixes can coexist as duplicate routes.
Multipath next-hop reorder produces a false mutation.
Route replace duplicates identity when metric/table normalization differs.
Two policy rules can claim the same effective priority.
A rule can reference a route table removed in the same revision.
Named-table aliases collide with reserved numeric tables.
A stale preview can apply after a newer revision.
Retrying an idempotency key creates a second transaction and audit event.
Readers observe desired revision metadata before all node plans publish.
Deleting a management route is accepted with no safe replacement.
A policy change diverts management CIDRs into an empty table.
Interface removal strands a protected gateway.
Mid-node apply failure leaves a partial observed snapshot.
Crash after desired publication loses rollback authority.
Rollback can use another node's last-known-good revision.
Equivalent multipath ordering is reported as drift.
An unowned observed route is scheduled for deletion.
Reconcile acts on an observed snapshot older than the latest apply.
A failed canary wave still allows the next wave.
Rollout retry reapplies nodes already at target revision.
An offline node is recorded successful from a stale heartbeat.
Ansible rerun rewrites unchanged config and restarts service.
Host protected routes are overwritten by group defaults.
A stale dashboard mutation overwrites a newer operator change.

organic_f2p_surface_assessment.rationale: Twenty-four manifestations across eight coupled root causes yield distinct safety, transaction, recovery, fleet, automation and UI behavior without padding.
